newsitem.title: GERMANY: Airlines set up German air cargo lobby grouping.
newsitem.headline: Airlines set up German air cargo lobby grouping.

text.p: Carriers in Germany have set up a new air cargo association as an intra-airline discussion forum and lobby grouping.
Dr Horst Bittlinger, general secretary of the Board of Airline Representatives in Germany (Barig), which has 102 airline members, said it has formed a Barig Cargo Committee (BCC).
An inaugural BCC meeting at Frankfurt airport was attended by representatives of 17 of the 31 airlines which have shown interest in the group, he told Reuters.
Air Canada Germany cargo manager Konrad Bossdorf was elected BCC chairman, with Edward Baradi, Germany cargo sales manager of Kuwait Airways as vice-chairman.
"Airlines demanded this committee and we hope they will use it and the Barig infrastructure. It is up to the airlines what they make of it," Bittlinger said.
A key subject at the first meeting was terms and conditions of airmail contracts with Deutsche Post AG and the new Frankfurt Airmail Centre, he added.

The committe will meet every three months and be attended by Airport Operators Committee (AOC) cargo chairman Reinhard Coldewe, German cargo manager of Emirates, and IATA's Germany manager, Winfried Stamer.
